evidence.excerpt: A two-dimensional finite-volume model of moisture and heat transport was developed for a generic polycarbonate housing representative of handheld electronic devices. The domain included the polymer shell, an internal air cavity of 38 cm³, and a printed circuit board heat source. Boundary conditions followed a 24-hour ambient cycle between 5 °C and 35 °C at 60–90 % relative humidity, representative of coastal storage conditions. The dew-point margin at the coldest internal surface was tracked over 72 simulated hours. For a housing wall thickness of 2 mm with no desiccant, the dew-point margin dropped below zero during the cooling phase at hour 14, predicting condensation on the board. Adding a 0.5 g silica gel insert raised the margin to +1.8 °C at the same instant. Model sensitivity to polycarbonate vapour diffusivity was assessed over a ±30 % range; the condensation-onset time varied by ±2.1 hours. The numerical approach is validated against laboratory cycling tests using thermocouples and a miniature humidity probe placed inside the cavity.
